title: Steve Jobs CNBC Interview, 5th Ave. Apple Store

content:
Glad to be here.

Well, you know, we we went into retail about five years ago. Opened our first store actually five years ago today. And um they've succeeded beyond our our our wildest dreams. Uh and one of the stores was here in Manhattan in Soho. And it was our most expensive store to build and we were a little little concerned that, you know, how much business would it do. And it it it uh it's just uh again, done phenomenal business. We've got so many Mac users here in New York and that store's gotten so crowded that we realized we had to open a second store in in New York City. And um we found this incredible location where uh the largest uh real estate developer in New York, uh Harry Macklowe had just bought the GM building. Uh and he he saw our Soho store and he said, you've got to be in in my new building. And we said, well, where do you have in mind? And he he said, well, underneath the plaza, there's some stores. And we said, subterranean? Are you crazy? But we called him back a day later and we said, we have this crazy idea. What if we could redo the plaza and make it this beautiful plaza, we'll put our store underneath it and we want an entrance right in the middle of the plaza. And he said, what kind of entrance? We said, how about a 32 foot glass cube? And he loved the idea and we got it through the city and we built it and it's it's opening tonight and we're pretty excited about it.

Well, you know, what's interesting is we we've never believed in the philosophy of having flagship stores that don't make money. Every single one of our stores uh makes money. And uh and so although we do spend a little more on these stores in New York, you know, the construction is more expensive and we also uh you know, they have to stand up to a lot of of use. Um they still do very well for us.

You know, one of the things we decided very early on was we wanted to provide great service to our customers. And so uh half the employee, we have 300 employees that will work in the store. Half of them are dedicated to things like our genius bar, which you can come in and for free get your questions answered, get your computers repaired, whatever you need, uh we try to take care of for you. And so we're we're highly service oriented. And it's gotten to the point with our Soho store where we open uh at 6 o'clock in the morning to serve people at the genius bar and we don't close till midnight. And we thought, you know, it isn't very much further to go where we could just try a store that's open 24 365. And uh so if you're, you know, you're working on your your your film editing and at 2 o'clock in the morning you've got a problem, we're going to be there for you.

Oh no, you know, I think uh again, we have partnerships with both Circuit City and Best Buy. Uh we sell primarily iPods through them. Uh but you can buy Macs in a lot of independent resellers. It's just that we want to invest more to make an even better buying experience. And I think the buying experience and the ownership experience of owning a Mac is is maybe the best of any product I know. And uh you know, it's because of the investment we're making in these stores and because of the passion we have for really taking care of our customers.

Well, you know, one of the advantages we have is is we have a market share of around 5% depending on which uh market research firm you listen to. And uh you know, you could say, well, that's that's that could be bigger and of course we'd like it to be bigger. One of the advantages is, you know, we've only got to convince 5% of the rest of the world to buy a Mac and we've doubled our market share. So clearly these stores we're hoping will help us grow our company. And indeed almost half the computers we sell in our stores are to people that have never owned a Mac before.

You know, we don't predict uh but we'll be glad to tell you uh how we're doing.

Um, well, iPods are extremely successful in the UK. Uh, and I think uh we are the number one MP3 player in France and Germany and many other countries in Europe, but we can always do better. And uh as you know, we sell, I think over 40% of our revenues uh come from international sales today. So we could do better than that, uh but I think we're doing pretty well now.

You know, um AMD's got some interesting products at the very high end of the server space. But the the part of the market that we concentrate on the most uh is notebooks and uh and consumer desktops. And for that, Intel's got the best chips. Uh this this Yona chip or the uh core duo that they have right now is the best chip in the world for notebooks and for consumer desktops. So right now, I think Intel's roadmap looks very, very strong for the kind of products uh the processors we we need to build the products that we build.

You know, we uh we never talk about unannounced products. So um if we ever do announce something like that, I'd love to talk to you about it then.

Thanks a lot.
